summary.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, led by manufacturing revenue up 20% to INR21,979 million, while trading revenue fell about 19% on Middle East disruption. EBITDA rose 5% to INR2,933 million, with margin down to 11.5%, and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 12.7%. Management reported a INR17,000 million QIP and the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27), and a run of new order wins across two-wheeler, renewable energy, and commercial vehicles. Management said cost pressures from steel, polymer, staff and energy have peaked and FY27 EBITDA margins should stay broadly stable versus FY26.

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; management said segment revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry growth of roughly 20-25%, attributed to customer mix.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; H-One high-tensile steel capability up to 1470 MPa cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.5% of manufacturing revenue; four-wheeler and CV revenue grew about 18% YoY per management opening remarks; Hyva India tipper acquisition announced 4 August 2026.

segments.name: Others (incl. aerospace, defence, renewables, trading)
segments.commentary: About 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Trading business fell about 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis and logistics; management expects mid-teens group revenue growth. Aerospace and defence target is at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins broadly stable versus FY26, with no material margin impact from input costs given back-to-back pricing.
Group revenue growth guided at mid-teens with stable EBITDA margins.
Majority of INR17,000 million QIP proceeds to be deployed within FY27, mainly for inorganic opportunities in aerospace and four-wheeler/CV, plus some organic growth.
Hyva India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27; deal to be EPS and ROCE accretive from day one per management's stated threshold.
Aerospace and defence to reach at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

New programs (chassis for fast-growing 2W OEM, US solar tracker assemblies, Sambhajinagar 2W chassis, brake assemblies) to start production in Q4 FY27; margin pressure expected to ease in coming quarters as pass-through takes effect.
capex_capacity: Four new facilities coming up, including brownfield facilities; fixed costs ramping ahead of revenue, per management.
Bangalore brownfield facility to host new 2W chassis program (annual revenue above INR650 million), SOP expected Q4 FY27.
US solar tracker sheet-metal assembly setup to support about 2.5 GW annual supplies; peak annual revenue above INR1,500 million; production from Q4 FY27.
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities to support a 59-assembly EV localisation program for a large Indian CV OEM.
Hyva acquisition includes three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.
Management declined to disclose utilisation or ramp-up details for specific facilities such as Bangalore and Haridwar.
demand_pricing: Order wins: 2W/3W chassis for fast-growing OEM (above INR650 million annual revenue, on top of about INR900 million fuel tank and exhaust win last quarter); cumulative about INR1,550 million with that OEM, about INR2,000 million including suspension and braking wins.
Suspension systems now supplied to five 2W/3W OEMs, including a new Vietnamese 2W entrant in India, with suspension and braking.
Two-wheeler chassis order for an existing model at a large 2W OEM's Sambhajinagar plant, potential annual revenue of about INR500 million.
Management attributed slower 2W/3W growth to a customer mix gap with faster-growing OEMs, with new OEM ramps expected in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Trading business decline was due to Middle East crisis hitting African, Asian and Middle Eastern demand and logistics; management says the worst is behind it.
Input cost pressure (steel, polymer, energy, logistics, minimum wage hike) persisted in Q1; management expects pass-through in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new chassis order additional to earlier two-wheeler wins from South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is over and above the exhaust and fuel tank win from last quarter (about INR900 million), making about INR1,550 million cumulative annual run-rate with that one OEM.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from commodities, staff costs and energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity, staff and energy/transport cost pressures have largely peaked, with staff cost rise tied to the annual increment cycle and pre-hiring for four new facilities; pass-through expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can management quantify the benefit from raw-material pass-through and the trading decline's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify either on the call and offered to respond offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did 2W/3W growth (about 18%) lag industry growth (about 20-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a customer mix issue, as some faster-growing OEMs it does not work with closely gained share; newly penetrated OEMs should add volumes in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aerospace and defence revenue outlook and the Plasan Sasa defence opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 10% of manufacturing revenue from aerospace and defence in the short-to-medium term; Belrise already exports parts to Plasan Sasa in Israel, with progress described as gradual given geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Can H-One and Mag Filters revenue be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said it manages the business as one group and will not disclose segment-level numbers for H-One or Mag Filters.

risks_watch: Margin recovery hinges on pass-through of steel, polymer and energy costs to OEMs in Q2-Q3 FY27; management did not quantify the benefit or the trading-decline effect on margin

Start-up costs from four new facilities (fixed costs ahead of revenue) could weigh on margins before new programs (Bangalore chassis, US solar tracker, Sambhajinagar chassis, brake assemblies) ramp in Q4 FY27
Execution and timing of the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27) and deployment of the INR17,000 million QIP mainly into inorganic aerospace and four-wheeler/CV deals
2W/3W growth (about 18%) lagged industry (about 20-25%); recovery depends on new OEM ramps in Q3-Q4 FY27
Trading business recovery after Middle East disruption; management says worst is behind but gave no specific guidance for the segment
Lack of disclosure: no utilisation or ramp data for specific facilities such as Bangalore and Haridwar, and no separate H-One or Mag Filters numbers; aerospace and defence revenue not carved out
key_quotes: I can say with a great amount of confidence that the worst is behind us in terms of cost pressures.
We are unable to comment on specific facilities. I think we have given our guidance on overall numbers and I think that's what we stick with.
We are unable to do that right now. We are happy to answer this question offline, but not at the moment.
We're unable to comment on specific numbers for either of them because for us, it's one whole family.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost trajectory and order momentum, with the CEO-level claim that the worst is behind on cost pressures and a firm mid-teens growth guide. Evasive on quantification: declined to size RM pass-through, margin impact of the trading decline, facility utilisation, and segment-level H-One or Mag Filters numbers, offering to answer offline.

growth.why: Management guides mid-teens group revenue growth with stable FY27 EBITDA margins, backed by named orders (2W chassis ~INR650m+, Sambhajinagar ~INR500m, solar tracker ~INR1,500m peak) and four new facilities, but utilisation and ramp details for specific plants were not disclosed and trading revenue fell ~19%.
